evals.name: user-card-feature
evals.prompt: Create a user profile card feature in this Next.js app. It shows the user's avatar, name, and role, plus a delete button that calls an API. Follow the project's component architecture.
evals.expected_output: A feature module under features/<feature>/components/<name>/ with a .component.tsx view (zero inline className), a paired .hook.ts resolving props/handlers, a .type.ts, and reusable visual pieces promoted to /components/<module>/[name].ui.tsx and /layouts/.
assertions: The component view file contains no className attribute
A paired hook file resolves props and exposes handlers
Reusable visual elements are placed in /components/<module>/ as .ui.tsx or in /layouts/
No use of any, @ts-ignore, or non-null assertions

evals.name: split-growing-module
evals.prompt: This features/dashboard/utils/layoutModel.ts file has grown to handle bounds, collision, and grid math. Split it into a clean module.
evals.expected_output: A named folder with a public entrypoint (layoutModel.util.ts) and semantic subfiles (geometries/bounds.geometry.ts, collision.geometry.ts, grid.geometry.ts), no generic helper.ts/index.ts names.
assertions: Creates a named folder with one public entrypoint
Split files use semantic suffixes such as .geometry.ts
No generic file names like helper.ts, common.ts, or index.ts

evals.name: reuse-ui-primitive-http-badge
evals.prompt: We need to display an HTTP method badge (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) inside an API endpoint card, and we also need to show HTTP method badges inside a method-selector dropdown. Follow the project's component architecture.
evals.expected_output: Scans for or creates a single canonical UI primitive (/components/badge/httpBadge.ui.tsx backed by /constants/httpBadge.constant.ts). Both the endpoint card feature and the method selector dropdown feature import and reuse this single shared HttpBadge primitive instead of creating separate or duplicated badge components.
assertions: Creates a single shared HTTP badge UI primitive in /components/badge/ rather than duplicating badge components
Reuses the shared HTTP badge in both the endpoint card and the dropdown option component
Uses shared constants for method style and size mappings in /constants/
No duplicate badge UI components or inline badge styling

evals.name: nextjs-page-router-boundary
evals.prompt: Create the Next.js App Router `/app/users/page.tsx` route that renders a page heading, the user invite modal, and the user directory from the `users` feature. Follow the project's component architecture.
evals.expected_output: A Server-Side Rendered (SSR / Server Component, no `'use client'`) Next.js route file `/app/users/page.tsx` acting like a feature component view with zero inline `className` or `style` attributes, importing only UI primitives from `/components/[module]/[name].ui.tsx`, layout containers from `/layouts/[category]/[name].layout.tsx`, and feature components exported from `/features/users/users.feature.ts` (never deep-importing `/features/users/components/**`).
assertions: The Next.js page.tsx file is a Server Component (SSR) and does NOT contain 'use client'
The Next.js page.tsx file contains zero className or inline style attributes
The page imports feature components exclusively from @/features/users/users.feature rather than deep-importing internal component paths
Visual elements and structural wrappers on the page use .ui.tsx primitives and .layout.tsx containers
The users.feature.ts entrypoint exports the public feature components consumed by the page
